The Science of Discworld intertwines two parallel storylines: one set in the fantastical world of Discworld, a flat planet carried on the backs of four elephants standing on a giant turtle swimming through space, and the other set in the real world, specifically centered around a science experiment being conducted at the Unseen University in Ankh-Morpork.

In Discworld, wizards of the Unseen University accidentally discover the ability to create a universe within a small bottle. This leads to the realization that the existence of the Discworld itself, with all its magic and fantastic creatures, is essentially a random experiment by the wizards of the Unseen University. They uncover the underlying principles that govern their universe and discover that their world is shaped by the power of narrative and belief.

Meanwhile, in the real world, renowned science writer Ian Stewart and acclaimed popular science author Jack Cohen examine how the principles of science in our universe are represented in the fantastical world of Discworld. As they explore the Discworld and its various landscapes, they explain complex scientific concepts in an accessible way, using examples from both worlds to illustrate their points.

The authors delve into diverse subjects such as evolution, biology, cosmology, and culture, offering a fresh perspective on how science and fiction can inform and enrich each other. Through their analysis, they challenge common scientific paradigms, exploring the role of imagination, the significance of stories, and the impact of belief systems in shaping our understanding of the universe.

The Science of Discworld seamlessly weaves together an imaginative narrative with real-world scientific explanations, entertaining and enlightening readers on the importance of scientific inquiry and the intricacies of the universe we inhabit. This compelling and thought-provoking novel encourages readers to embrace the wonder of both science and fiction, as each holds its own unique power to shape our view of the world.

The BBC should not be "complacent" about the future and must not allow its standards to slip, Business Secretary Peter Mandelson has warned.

In a speech to the Royal Television Society, he said the BBC was "the envy of the world" but it must not take its success for granted.

He also said the BBC must not be seen to be "on the side of the government" and should be "fearless" in its journalism.

The BBC is facing criticism from some quarters over its handling of the MPs' expenses scandal.

'Innovation and creativity'

Mr Mandelson told the RTS Cambridge Convention that the BBC was "the envy of the world" and "a great British institution".

But he warned: "The BBC must not be complacent about its future and it must not allow its standards to slip.

"The BBC must continue to innovate and be creative. It must not be seen to be on the side of the government, but it must also be fearless in its journalism."

The BBC is facing criticism from some quarters - including some MPs - over its handling of the MPs' expenses scandal.

But Mr Mandelson said the BBC had "played a vital role" in exposing the scandal and that it was "right" that it had done so.

He also defended the BBC's decision to screen footage of the Queen apparently storming out of a photoshoot with Annie Leibovitz, saying it was in the public interest.

'Diversity and choice'

Mr Mandelson also used his speech to defend the government's plans to part-fund the rollout of super-fast broadband across the UK.

He said the government was not trying to "pick winners" but wanted to ensure there was "diversity and choice" in the broadband market.

The government has come under fire from some quarters for its plans to invest £530m in the rollout of super-fast broadband.

Critics have accused the government of trying to "pick winners" and of favouring BT over other providers.

But Mr Mandelson said the government was not trying to "pick winners" and that it wanted to ensure there was "diversity and choice" in the broadband market.

He also said the government was not trying to "micromanage" the BBC and that it was "not for the government to tell the BBC what to do".

I am not sure if I have ever been so happy as when I was in my garden,

And all around me were the flowers and trees that had grown there for years.

They were beautiful, they were fragrant, they were alive with life.

There was no one else here but me, and I could see them all.

It was like being in a dream, or in some other world where everything was perfect.

But then I remembered something, and it made me sad.

I remember how I used to love to go out into the woods and play.

When I was young, I would climb up on the branches of these trees,

And sit down by the stream and listen to the birds sing.

Now I don't know what happened, but somehow I lost this feeling.

Maybe it's because I've never really been alone.

Or maybe it's just because I'm afraid of the dark.

So I stay inside, and I keep myself busy with work.

Sometimes I think about going outside again, but I can't seem to find the courage.

I guess I'll just have to wait until I get older.

A Dream Of Foxes  
by Niki de Saint Phalle
I was afraid of being alone
and I called the foxes to watch me.
They came and licked me and said:
"It is true you are just a body
no more a goddess
but you will not be lonely."
And I said,
"No, I will not be lonely."
And a fox bit my finger
and showed me his fangs and said:
"It is true your body is not made of gold
but it is still shining."
And I said,
"No, my body is not shining."
And a fox bit my arm
and showed me blood
and said:
"The moon is full and shining like your body
as the stars are bright like your eyes."
And I said,
"No, my eyes are not bright like the stars."
And I cried.
And the foxes were happy,
because they like to watch
your tears while you cry.
They are like stars, like your eyes.
They are like shining, like your body
as they are like blood, like your scars.

1/2 cup butter

1/2 cup white sugar

1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder

1/2 cup all-purpose flour

1/2 cup chopped walnuts

1/2 cup sweetened condensed milk

1/2 cup instant coffee granules

1/2 cup confectioners' sugar

In a small saucepan, combine the white chocolate chips, condensed milk and instant coffee. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until smooth. Pour over the chocolate chips. Refrigerate until firm.

Remove from refrigerator and sprinkle with confectioners' sugar. Cut into bars."

In this paper, we demonstrate a novel approach for optically addressing a single erbium ion in a silicon crystal using a focused laser beam. Erbium ions are incorporated into the silicon lattice through a process known as implantation, and their unique optical properties make them suitable for quantum information processing and other photonic applications.

Current methods for addressing individual erbium ions in silicon rely on electrical techniques, which can be limited by the difficulty in precisely controlling the position of the ion and the electric field strength. Our proposed optical approach offers several advantages, including high spatial resolution, low power consumption, and the ability to address multiple ions simultaneously.

We experimentally demonstrate the ability to optically address a single erbium ion in silicon using a focused laser beam with a radius of approximately 1 micrometer. By tuning the laser frequency to the ion's resonant transition, we observe a clear signature of ion-photon interaction, indicating successful addressing of the individual ion.

Our results pave the way for the development of scalable, densely-packed arrays of individually-addressable erbium ions in silicon, which could enable a new generation of quantum information processing and photonic devices. By leveraging the unique properties of rare-earth ions in silicon, this work contributes to the development of a promising platform for quantum computing and other photonic applications.

The European Parliament has ordered a reboot of its ambitious plans to create a unified patent system across Europe.

The assembly's legal affairs committee said the package, known as the unitary patent, would be rewritten to try to address critics' concerns.

These centred on the involvement of the European Court of Justice, the need for translation and whether patents would be valid in all EU states.

The legislation aims to simplify patent protection by allowing inventors to gain patent protection in a single, unified patent court.

The legislation has faced resistance from Italy, Spain and Poland. They have threatened to block the legislation unless changes are made.

The committee said it planned to split the unitary patent package into two bills.

One would deal with the unitary patent itself while the other would establish a new court to handle patent disputes, known as the Unified Patent Court (UPC).

Italian socialist Guido Sacconi, who led the work on the report, said the committee had decided to "take the bull by the horns".

"We have decided to modify the two pillars of the unitary patent package: the unitary patent itself and the Unified Patent Court," he said.

"The two elements will be split and this will allow us to proceed with the patent court and a bit later discuss the unitary patent."

The committee's proposal will now go before the full parliament for a vote.

If passed, it will then be up to the EU's 28 member states to decide whether to proceed with the plan.

Currently, inventors must apply for patent protection in each EU country where they want patent protection.

The court would have the power to rule on patent disputes for the entire EU, making it easier for inventors to protect their patents across the EU.

In this study, we investigate the time complexity of synchronizing a collection of discrete pulse-coupled oscillators (PCOs) operating on a tree topology. PCO networks have long been used to model and control biological systems, such as heartbeat regulation and animal locomotion. However, their effectiveness is heavily dependent on the ability to synchronize the individual oscillators, which remains an open research challenge. Despite extensive work in this area, it has not yet been established what determines the efficiency of different algorithms in accomplishing this task.

In this context, we analyze two popular algorithms for synchronization: the Kuramoto algorithm and its variants based on spectral theory. Both these algorithms are known to operate with linear time complexity, which implies that they can be easily scaled up to handle large numbers of coupled oscillators. We demonstrate how their convergence properties depend on various parameters of the system (such as coupling strength and initial conditions), using both numerical simulations and theoretical analyses. Our results suggest that the efficient operation of these algorithms requires careful tuning of these parameter values. Additionally, we observe that certain structural characteristics of the network (e.g., clustering coefficients and path lengths) also play a crucial role in determining their performance.

Herbed Egg 'Pasta' With Blood Orange Salsa and Lettuce Slaw Recipe

Ingredients:

- 4 large eggs
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon dried basil
- 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 small red onion, thinly sliced
- 2 blood oranges, peeled and segmented
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- 2 tablespoon fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tablespoon fresh mint, chopped
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
- 8 large leaves of butter lettuce, torn into bite-sized pieces
- 1 avocado, diced

Instructions:

1. In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs, salt, pepper, basil and oregano until well combined.

2. Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Pour the egg mixture into the skillet, swirling to coat the bottom of the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes until the eggs start to set.

3. Use a spatula to gently lift and fold the eggs, continue to cook for another 2-3 minutes until the eggs are cooked through but still slightly runny.

4. In a separate bowl, combine the red onion, blood orange segments, red bell pepper, cherry tomatoes, parsley, mint, and lime juice to make the blood orange salsa.

5. In another bowl, combine the butter lettuce and diced avocado to make the lettuce slaw.

6. Divide the egg 'pasta' onto plates, spoon the blood orange salsa over the top, and serve with the lettuce slaw on the side.

7. Garnish with extra parsley and mint if desired.

Enjoy your delicious and healthy Herbed Egg 'Pasta' With Blood Orange Salsa and Lettuce Slaw!
